title: Onboarding contract for unpinned open-model variants and automated rollback criteria
creator: Noah Williams
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines the product contract and acceptance criteria for onboarding new open-model variants into the public model catalog when a variant is not automatically pinned to a specific runtime build. The goal is a machine-checkable compatibility surface and a deterministic escalation/rollback policy so that unpinned community weights can be served safely without surprising customers or causing runtime regressions.

Problem statement:
- Community model variants arrive with varying metadata quality and can break runtime optimizations (e.g. KV cache shape, attention kernels).
- Current onboarding guidance is vague on when a model variant should be pinned vs left unpinned; engineers manually triage causing delays.
- Customers experience intermittent latency regressions and OOMs when runtime attempts aggressive optimizations against untested variants.

Goals:
- Define a compact compatibility schema that the intake system and runtime compiler can validate pre-merge.
- Establish deterministic rules that decide when a variant must be pinned, can be unpinned, or requires gated rollout.
- Provide automatic fallback/rollback triggers tied to observable signals (latency, error rate, memory growth).
- Ensure model catalog UI/API surface exposes compatibility badges and pin status.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting runtime kernel selection logic (ENG work ticket will be separate).
- Automated model performance tuning — out of scope for this ticket.
requirements: Create a machine-readable compatibility_schema for all model entries (see compatibility_schema field).
Intake UI and API must reject a model upload missing required fields in the compatibility_schema with a clear validation error.
Define a deterministic pinning_policy that maps metadata + test-run results to one of: pinned, unpinned, gated-rollout.
Implement an automated rollback policy: runtime will mark a model variant unhealthy if it exceeds thresholds and initiate a fallback to the nearest compatible pinned variant or prior stable variant.
Catalog UI should render a compatibility status badge: Compatible / Partial / Incompatible and show reason text from compatibility notes.
Provide a preflight test harness (small synthetic runs) that returns a standardized test report used by intake to decide gating/pinning.
Document developer playbook for manually requesting an exception (temporary unpinned opt-out) and required review steps.
Expose telemetry events for onboarding decisions (pin/unpin/gate/rollback) to the catalog analytics pipeline for monitoring and reporting.
compatibility_schema: tokenizer: tokenizer family id (e.g., hf-bpe, tiktoken)
preferred_quant_profiles: list of strings (int8, int4, fp16), optional
runtime_notes: freeform short string for edge-case compatibility notes
compatibility_score_estimate: numeric string between '0' and '100' produced by preflight harness
pinning_policy: - If preflight harness returns compatibility_score_estimate < 60 => pin required.
- If recommended_sequence_profiles does not include 'short' and median request length for tenant workloads is < 512 tokens => pin recommended (runtime risk).
- compatibility_score_estimate >= 85 and kv_cache_compatible == 'yes' and quant profiles include at least one supported profile in runtime (e.g., fp16/int8).
Gated-rollout conditions: when score between 60-84 or tokenizer mismatch risk; rollout at 5% traffic with 1-week observation window.
- Error rate increase > 3x baseline sustained for 10 minutes triggers immediate fallback and marks variant unhealthy.
- P50 latency increase > 2x baseline for 5 minutes triggers rollback to pinned variant.
- Memory/GPU OOM incidents for a given host group trigger immediate quarantine and pinning of variant for that customer until manual review.
Escalation: automated rollback generates a ticket and notifies on-call runtime engineer + PM + uploader email; the variant is flagged in the catalog as 'quarantined' until triage.
acceptance_criteria: Intake API validation returns descriptive error for any missing required compatibility_schema field.
Preflight harness integrated into intake pipeline and produces compatibility_score_estimate for every new variant upload.
Pinning decision is deterministic and recorded as a single catalog field 'pin_status' with values [pinned, unpinned, gated].
Catalog UI surfaces compatibility badge, pin_status, and a short runtime_notes blurb for every variant.
Automated rollback triggers have unit and integration tests; a synthetic failure in test harness simulates error-rate spike and causes fallback to previous pinned variant in staging.
Telemetry emitted to analytics pipeline for all onboarding decisions and rollback events (events contain variant_id, decision, reason_code).
Product documentation and developer playbook updated and linked from the intake UI 'help' section.
decisions: Use a numeric compatibility_score_estimate from the preflight harness as the primary heuristic for pin decisions.
Compatibility schema must be strict on kv_cache_compatible and max_context_tokens to allow static checks in runtime compiler selection.
Gated-rollout default is 5% traffic for 7 days unless a customer requests otherwise with documented approval.
Pinning is a property of a variant, not a model family; pinning may be programmatically lifted only after a full re-run of the preflight harness and a manual approval flow.
